# Project Tracker

appgen generated this REST API from the app definition `project-tracker`,
with the FastAPI binding. Do not edit the generated files: change the app
definition, and run `appgen generate` again. Write your own code in the
extension files (`*_ext.py`), which appgen creates once and never
changes:

- `<operation>_ext.py`: the logic of a custom operation. Until you write
  it, the endpoint gives 501.
- `validation_ext.py`: the rules that the create and update operations
  check before they store a record. By default, it accepts all records.

When you write the code of an extension file, change `@trace:gap` to
`@trace:manual` in its header.

## Stack

- FastAPI 0.161 on Python 3.14
- Vertical slice architecture
- SQLAlchemy 2 (async), Alembic, and Postgres (SQLite for local runs)
- uv

## Commands

| Task               | Command                                   |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| Install            | `uv sync`                                 |
| Migrate the database | `uv run alembic upgrade head`           |
| Start the API      | `uv run fastapi dev app/main.py`          |
| Lint               | `uv run ruff check`                       |
| Check the format   | `uv run ruff format --check`              |
| Type check         | `uv run pyright`                          |
| Test               | `uv run pytest`                           |
| Run with Docker    | `docker compose up --build`               |

The API documentation is at `/docs` when the API runs. The API reads
its settings from environment variables or from a `.env` file (see
`.env.example`), for example `DATABASE_URL`.

## Local database

To run the API without a Postgres server, use SQLite. Write the URL
into `.env`, then migrate the database and start the API:

```sh
printf 'DATABASE_URL=sqlite+aiosqlite:///./local.db\n' > .env
uv run alembic upgrade head
uv run fastapi dev app/main.py
```

The API and Alembic read `DATABASE_URL` from `.env` or from an
exported environment variable. A shell variable that you do not export
has no effect.

The database is the file `local.db`. The models and the migrations work
on both databases. Use Postgres in production: SQLite has one writer at
a time, and it stores the date and time values in UTC.

## Schema changes

appgen creates the first migration (`migrations/versions/0001_schema.py`)
once, and a new run of appgen keeps all migrations. To change the schema
of a database that has data:

1. Change the app definition, and generate the app again into this
   folder.
2. Make the next migration from the changed models. Alembic compares
   the models with the database of `DATABASE_URL`:

   ```sh
   uv run alembic revision --autogenerate -m "add the phone of a person"
   ```

3. Review the new file in `migrations/versions/`. Alembic does not find
   all changes: edit the migration for a rename (Alembic gives a drop
   and an add) or for a changed enum value.
4. Apply it: `uv run alembic upgrade head`. The data stays.

## Tests

The tests need a database. By default, they start Postgres in a container
with Testcontainers, so Docker must run. To use a database that runs
already, or SQLite, set `TEST_DATABASE_URL`, for example to
`sqlite+aiosqlite:///./test.db`. The tests delete all data in it.

Each operation has a test module in `tests/features/<slice>/`, with
the success case and the main error cases. The factories in
`tests/factories.py` give valid input and store records, with the
records that they need. The generated tests of a custom operation check
only its errors (404 and 422). Write the tests of its logic in your own
test modules, which appgen does not change.

## Docker

`docker compose up --build` builds the image, starts Postgres, runs the
migrations, and starts the API on port 8000. The Dockerfile installs
the dependencies with uv in a build stage, and runs the API as a
non-root user. To use other images, for example from a mirror, set the
build arguments `UV_IMAGE` and `PYTHON_IMAGE`, and the environment
variable `POSTGRES_IMAGE` for Compose.

## Production

- Logs: the API writes one log line for each request, with the method,
  the path, the status, the duration, and a request ID (the
  `X-Request-ID` header, or a new ID). `LOG_JSON=true` (the default)
  writes each line as a JSON object, and `LOG_LEVEL` sets the lowest
  level.
- Rate limits: `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` sets the number of requests that
  each client address can send in each minute (0, the default, sets no
  limit). Over the limit, the API gives 429 with `Retry-After`. The
  counts are in the memory of each process, so each replica has its own
  limit. `/health` has no limit.
- Kubernetes: `deploy/kubernetes/` has a Kustomize folder with a
  Deployment (2 replicas, a non-root user, a read-only file system), a
  Service, and a Job that runs the migrations. The database is outside
  the cluster. Push the image, set its name in `kustomization.yaml`,
  copy `secret.example.env` to `secret.env`, and set the values. Then
  run `kubectl delete job project-tracker-migrate --ignore-not-found` and
  `kubectl apply -k deploy/kubernetes`.

## Layout

Each entity of the definition is a vertical slice: one folder with all
the code of the feature.

| Folder                  | Content                                              |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `app/main.py`           | The entry point. It adds the router of each slice.   |
| `app/models.py`         | Imports the models of all slices.                    |
| `app/core/`             | Code that all slices share: settings, database, errors, pagination, health, and schema bases. |
| `migrations/`           | The Alembic migrations.                              |
| `app/features/<slice>/` | One slice for each entity.                           |
| `tests/`                | The tests, with one folder for each slice.           |

A slice has these modules:

| Module              | Content                                                     |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `router.py`         | The router of the slice. It adds the router of each operation. |
| `models.py`         | The SQLAlchemy model: the table, its columns, and relations. |
| `schemas.py`        | The Pydantic schemas: create, update, read, and the params of the custom operations. |
| `enums.py`          | The enums of the enum fields and params, if the entity has some. |
| `repository.py`     | The data access that the operations share.                  |
| `<operation>.py`    | One module for each CRUD or list operation: its endpoint and its handler. |
| `<operation>_gen.py` | The endpoint of a custom operation.                        |
| `<operation>_ext.py` | The logic of a custom operation. Write it here.            |
| `validation_ext.py` | The custom validation of the entity. Write it here.        |

## Errors and pages

All errors use the problem details format of RFC 9457, with the media
type `application/problem+json`. A request with values that are not
valid gives 422, with one item for each error. A record that does not
exist gives 404. A change that breaks a unique value or a reference gives
409. A custom operation without logic gives 501.

List endpoints take `limit` (default 50), `offset`, and `sort`. The
`sort` value is a list of sort keys, separated by commas. A `-` before
a key sorts in descending order, for example `sort=-due_date,title`.
Empty values come last. The sort keys are the fields with a simple type,
and the sortable columns and the sort of the views, for example `owner`
(the display field of the related record) or `project.name`.
List endpoints also take one equality filter for each field with a
simple type, for example `done=true`. The filters of the views add more
parameters:

| Filter of a view | Parameters | Example |
| ---------------- | ---------- | ------- |
| `select`         | The field takes one or more values. | `status=todo&status=done` |
| `boolean`        | The field takes `true` or `false`. | `active=true` |
| `date_range`     | `<field>_from` and `<field>_to`: the first and the last day. | `due_date_from=2026-01-01` |
| `search`         | `q`: each word is in one of the fields of the search filters. | `q=alpha` |

A field path of a view keeps its dots, for example `project.status=active`.
A tab of a detail view that lists the records of a many-to-many relation
adds `id`, a list of record IDs, to the list endpoint of the target.
An unknown parameter, value, or sort key gives 422. The response has the
`items` and the `total` number of records.
